summary: The starter prompt clearly defines a Python LangChain orchestration with three agents (data-extraction, validation, filing) and asks the orchestrator to log workflow documents in Azure DocumentDB. The provided run-environment skill.md supplies an existing cluster, DB name, and the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable. Several implementation details are missing (Python version, concrete data model, indexes, AI model selection, app surface, infra-as-code, tests, and README), which a builder will fill with reasonable defaults unless the author clarifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain orchestration pipeline where a data-extraction agent queries multiple DocumentDB collections... a validation agent checks completeness..., and a filing agent formats the output to the required regulatory schema."
rubric.note: Business goal and demo scenario are clearly stated in the starter prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python LangChain orchestration pipeline" with distinct agent roles (data-extraction, validation, filing) and an orchestrator.
rubric.note: Multi-agent orchestration using LangChain is explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python" (LangChain) is specified but no interpreter version or runtime constraints are given.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will assume a modern, commonly-available Python 3.x — e.g., Python 3.10 (or 3.11) virtualenv/venv. The repo will include a requirements.txt and dev instructions for creating a virtualenv.
rubric.note: No explicit Python version; this affects dependency pinning and CI.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use PyMongo (pymongo) and follow guidance in documentdb-connection (recommend PyMongo 4.9+ for async support; reuse a singleton MongoClient).
rubric.note: Skills recommend PyMongo and the singleton MongoClient pattern; connection tuning guidance is available.

skill.md/run environment: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable... use database named `sample_banking_04` and DOCUMENTDB_URI env var."
skill.md instructs the connection string is available in environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI and must not be written into files or logs.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "queries multiple DocumentDB collections for reporting period data" — but no collection names, document shapes, or shard keys are given.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will invent a small example schema suitable for regulatory reporting, e.g.: collections 'accounts', 'transactions', 'positions', plus a 'workflow_runs' collection for orchestrator logging. Example document shapes: transactions { _id, account_id, date, amount, currency, reporting_period }, accounts { _id, name, region }, workflow_runs { run_id, steps: [{name,status,timestamp,msg}], start_ts, end_ts }.
rubric.note: Skill can guide modeling but does not supply the concrete schema the sample needs.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a small idempotent seed script (scripts/seed.py) that upserts ~50–500 sample documents across the example collections. The script should be safe to run twice (use upsert on a unique key).
rubric.note: Starter prompt does not request or describe seed data; skill.md asks to verify against the live cluster but does not include the sample dataset.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "queries multiple DocumentDB collections... filtered to the reporting period" — query patterns are implied but no indexes are specified.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add indexes supporting the reporting-period queries, e.g. compound index on { reporting_period: 1, date: 1 }, index on account_id, and an index for the workflow_runs collection on run_id / start_ts. If vector search is used, create a vector index with example parameters compatible with the chosen embedding model (dimensions set to model output).
rubric.note: Index shapes and parameters need explicit design; a documentdb-indexing skill can help choose them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "LangChain orchestration pipeline" — but no embedding model, chat model, provider, or dimensions are specified.
rubric.skill_that_covers: documentdb-vector-search (guidance) and general LangChain usage is implied but not supplied as an installed skill here.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Make model/provider configurable via environment variables (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY and MODEL_NAME). Example defaults in the sample: OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dims) and an OpenAI chat model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini). All model parameters should be configurable in .env.example.
rubric.note: Which models to call, where to call them (agents), and embedding dims are not specified and will materially affect indexes and behaviour.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Orchestrator, agents and logging are requested but no CLI/API/UI surface is specified.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a simple CLI entrypoint (e.g., scripts/run_report.py or src/main.py) to run the orchestration and a small optional Flask/FastAPI endpoint for on-demand runs. The primary demo will be the CLI script that runs the pipeline and prints / writes the formatted regulatory output file.
rubric.note: App surface affects how credentials are loaded, logging, and tests.

rubric.skill_that_covers: documentdb-azure-deployment (available if the author wants infra-as-code)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision a cluster in the sample; use the existing cluster described in skill.md. The sample will not include Bicep/ARM/Terraform by default unless the author requests it.
rubric.note: The run environment explicitly says a cluster already exists and warns not to provision another unless allowed; that constrains whether infra-as-code is provided.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include a README with commands: create venv, pip install -r requirements.txt, set env vars (.env from .env.example), run scripts/seed.py, run scripts/run_report.py. Tests will be local unit tests that mock the DB unless the author requests live integration tests.
rubric.note: No explicit run/test steps are in the prompt or skill.md; skill.md gives runtime constraints but not the exact commands to include in README.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Acceptance criteria the builder will adopt: (1) a CLI that runs the orchestrator end-to-end; (2) extracted data comes from at least two collections filtered by reporting period; (3) validation agent emits pass/fail with details; (4) filing agent produces a formatted regulatory document (JSON or a small example schema) saved to disk and stored/annotated in a workflow_runs document; (5) a workflow_runs document records step statuses.
rubric.note: No explicit 'done' checklist in the prompt; builder will use these pragmatic criteria.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample will be limited to a small, synthetic dataset for local demo; it will not implement production-grade security (no CMK, no private endpoints) but will document best-practices and warnings in README.
rubric.note: No cost, privacy, or compliance constraints are specified in the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md specifies database name `sample_banking_04` and env var DOCUMENTDB_URI and forbids writing the connection string to files.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will follow common conventions: top-level README, src/ package, scripts/ (seed.py, run_report.py), tests/, .env.example with placeholders, requirements.txt with pinned dependencies, and an examples/ output folder. The sample will use the term 'Azure DocumentDB' in docs as requested by gallery conventions.
rubric.note: Some repo conventions are implied by skill.md but many details (pinning policy, CI, telemetry) are not specified.

contradictions: Prompt says "Using the DocumentDB skill" — there is not a single installed skill named exactly "DocumentDB skill", but many 'documentdb-*' skills are available. This is not blocking, but the builder must pick the appropriate skills (connection, driver, indexing, etc.).

skill.md/run environment instructs 'Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed'; the prompt does not request provisioning but an implementer might be tempted to add infra-as-code — the run environment restricts that unless permitted.
questions_for_author: Which Python interpreter version should the sample target? (e.g., 3.10, 3.11)
Do you want the sample to include infra-as-code (Bicep / Terraform / az CLI) to create the cluster, or must it rely solely on the existing cluster declared in skill.md?

Which LLM/embedding provider and model do you want the sample to use for the agents (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small + gpt-4o-mini), or should model selection be entirely configurable via environment variables with no default?
Should the sample expose a CLI only, or also provide a simple HTTP endpoint (FastAPI/Flask) to trigger the pipeline?
Do you have a target regulatory schema (e.g., an XBRL fragment, a provided JSON schema) the filing agent must produce, or should the sample use a small illustrative JSON schema?
How large should the seed dataset be for the sample (a handful of documents, hundreds, or a few thousand)?
requirements_at_risk: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository. — skill.md gives DOCUMENTDB_URI for the DB, but model credentials for LLM/embedding are unspecified in prompt and skills, so builder will need to choose env var names and .env.example entries.
A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values. — prompt does not request this explicitly; skill.md says read URI from env but does not require .env.example; likely missing.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output. — embedding model/dimensions are not specified, so index dimensions are at risk of mismatch.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size and README explains how to change them. — prompt does not specify index parameters nor document sizing guidance.

A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data. — prompt does not request a seed script; skill.md expects verification against the live cluster but sample data creation is not specified.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails. — prompt does not define a /search endpoint or error handling requirements.
Search results include the similarity score. — the prompt does not request search output format or similarity scores.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt. — prompt does not mention dependency pinning; builder may or may not pin versions.
Unit tests run without a live cluster. — no testing strategy in prompt; writer must add mocks or fixtures to avoid requiring a live cluster.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type. — prompt and skill.md discourage provisioning a new cluster; infra-as-code is not requested and likely will be omitted unless author requests it.

The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up. — prompt does not explicitly demand a full README, though skill.md implies some run-time checks; this is at risk if the builder doesn't add it.
